source: E-MU Mo Phatt Operation Manual pp. 133-135, Filter Types table. Raw extraction: ref/mophatt_zplane_pages_extracted.txt (quote from that file; this file only reverses documented glyph damage).
restoration: PDF extraction damage reversed and nothing else: 'Þ'→'fi', 'ß'→'fl', 'Ò'/'Ó'→straight quotes, 'Õ'→apostrophe, dropped leading capitals restored from the known filter names (e.g. 'alkingHedz'→'TalkingHedz', 'owel'→'Vowel', 'T y'→'Try', 'iolent'→'Violent'), kerning splits closed ('T weeters'→'Tweeters').

filters.name: Smooth
filters.sentence: Typical OB type low-pass filter with a shallow 12 dB/octave slope.

filters.name: Classic
filters.sentence: 4-pole low-pass filter, the standard filter on classic analog synths. 24 dB/octave rolloff.

filters.name: Steeper
filters.sentence: 6-pole low-pass filter which has a steeper slope than a 4-pole low-pass filter. 36 dB/octave rolloff!

filters.name: MegaSweepz
filters.sentence: "Loud" LPF with a hard Q. Tweeters beware!

filters.name: EarlyRizer
filters.sentence: Classic analog sweeping with hot Q and Lo-end.

filters.name: Millennium
filters.sentence: Aggressive low-pass filter. Q gives you a variety of spiky tonal peaks.

filters.name: KlubKlassik
filters.sentence: Responsive low-pass filter sweep with a wide spectrum of Q sounds

filters.name: BassBox-303
filters.sentence: Pumped up lows with TB-like squelchy Q factor.

filters.name: Shallow
filters.sentence: 2-pole high-pass filter. 12 dB/octave slope.

filters.name: Deeper
filters.sentence: Classic 4-pole high-pass filter. Cutoff sweep progressively cuts 4th Order High-pass.

filters.name: Band-pass1
filters.sentence: Band-pass filter with 6 dB/octave rolloff on either side of the passband and Q control.

filters.name: Band-pass2
filters.sentence: Band-pass filter with 12 dB/octave rolloff on either side of the passband and Q control.

filters.name: ContraBand
filters.sentence: A novel band-pass filter where the frequency peaks and dips midway in the frequency range.

filters.name: Swept1>1oct
filters.sentence: Parametric filter with 24 dB of boost or cut and a one octave bandwidth.

filters.name: Swept2>1oct
filters.sentence: Parametric filter with 24 dB of boost or cut. The bandwidth of the filter is two octaves wide at the low end of the audio spectrum, gradually changing to one octave wide at the upper end of the spectrum.

filters.name: Swept3>1oct
filters.sentence: Parametric filter with 24 dB of boost or cut. The bandwidth of the filter is three octaves wide at the low end of the audio spectrum, gradually changing to one octave wide at the upper end of the spectrum.

filters.name: DJAlkaline
filters.sentence: Band accentuating filter, Q shifts "ring" frequency

filters.name: AceOfBass
filters.sentence: Bass-boost to bass-cut morph

filters.name: TB-OrNot-TB
filters.sentence: Great Bassline "Processor."

filters.name: BolandBass
filters.sentence: Constant bass boost with mid-tone Q control.

filters.name: BassTracer
filters.sentence: Low Q boosts bass. Try sawtooth or square waveform with Q set to 115.

filters.name: RogueHertz
filters.sentence: Bass with mid-range boost and smooth Q. Sweep cutoff with Q at 127.

filters.name: RazorBlades
filters.sentence: Cuts a series of frequency bands. Q selects different bands.

filters.name: RadioCraze
filters.sentence: Band limited for a cheap radio-like EQ

filters.name: AahAyEeh
filters.sentence: Vowel formant filter which sweeps from "Ah" sound, through "Ay" sound to "Ee" sound at maximum frequency setting. Q varies the apparent size of the mouth cavity

filters.name: Ooh-To-Aah
filters.sentence: Vowel formant filter which sweeps from "Oo" sound, through "Oh" sound to "Ah" sound at maximum frequency setting. Q varies the apparent size of mouth cavity

filters.name: MultiQVox
filters.sentence: Multi-Formant, Map Q velocity

filters.name: Ooh-To-Eee
filters.sentence: Oooh to Eeee formant morph.

filters.name: TalkingHedz
filters.sentence: "Oui" morphing filter. Q adds peaks.

filters.name: Eeh-To-Aah
filters.sentence: "E" to "Ah" formant movement. Q accentuates "peakiness."

filters.name: UbuOrator
filters.sentence: Aah-Uuh vowel with no Q. Raise Q for throaty vocals.

filters.name: DeepBouche
filters.sentence: French vowels! "Ou-Est" vowel at low Q.

filters.name: PhazeShift1
filters.sentence: Recreates a comb filter effect typical of phase shifters. Frequency moves position of notches. Q varies the depth of the notches.

filters.name: PhazeShift2
filters.sentence: Comb filter with slightly different notch frequency moving the frequency of notches. Q varies the depth of the notches.

filters.name: FreakShifta
filters.sentence: Phasey movement. Try major 6 interval and maximum Q.

filters.name: CruzPusher
filters.sentence: Accentuates harmonics at high Q. Try with a sawtooth LFO.

filters.name: FlangerLite
filters.sentence: Contains three notches. Frequency moves frequency and spacing of notches. Q increases flanging depth.

filters.name: AngelzHairz
filters.sentence: Smooth sweep flanger. Good with vox waves. eg. I094, Q =60

filters.name: DreamWeava
filters.sentence: Directional Flanger. Poles shift down at low Q and up at high Q.

filters.name: MeatyGizmo
filters.sentence: Filter inverts at mid-Q.

filters.name: DeadRinger
filters.sentence: Permanent "Ringy" Q response. Many Q variations.

filters.name: ZoomPeaks
filters.sentence: High resonance nasal filter

filters.name: AcidRavage
filters.sentence: Great analog Q response. Wide tonal range. Try with a sawtooth LFO.

filters.name: BassOMatic
filters.sentence: Low boost for basslines. Q goes to distortion at the maximum level.

filters.name: LucifersQ
filters.sentence: Violent mid Q filter! Take care with Q values 40-90.

filters.name: ToothComb
filters.sentence: Highly resonant harmonic peaks shift in unison. Try mid Q.

filters.name: EarBender
filters.sentence: Midway between wah & vowel. Strong mid-boost. Nasty at high Q settings.

filters.name: FuzziFace
filters.sentence: Nasty clipped distortion. Q functions as mid-frequency tone control.

filters.name: BlissBatz
filters.sentence: Bat phaser from the Emulator 4.

filters.name: KlangKling
filters.sentence: Ringing Flange filter. Q "tunes" the ring frequency.
